title: K-injective derived direct-image comparisons for subterminal slices
statement:
Let $(\mathcal E,J)$ be a small subcanonical site with finite limits, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ subterminal objects; no covering hypothesis is imposed. Put $W=U\times V$. Use the module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on $\mathcal E$ and its localized ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $j_Z^*$ for restriction to $Z=U,V,W$ and $k_U^*,k_V^*$ for restriction to $W$ within the $U,V$ slices. All these module categories admit K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Restriction and its underived right adjoint preserve K-injective complexes. On module sheaves this right adjoint is
$$(j_{Z*}F)(C)=F(C\times Z\to Z),$$
with $R(C)$ acting by restriction to $R(C\times Z)$; $k_{U*},k_{V*}$ have the same formula inside the slices. Thus $j_Z^*\dashv Rj_{Z*}$ on unbounded derived categories, and $Rj_{Z*}(Q I)=Q(j_{Z*}I)$ for every K-injective complex $I$ on the slice, where $Q$ denotes localization. There are natural derived identifications
$$j_U^*Rj_{U*}A\cong A,\quad j_U^*Rj_{V*}B\cong Rk_{U*}(k_V^*B),\quad j_U^*Rj_{W*}D\cong Rk_{U*}D,$$
$$j_V^*Rj_{V*}B\cong B,\quad j_V^*Rj_{U*}A\cong Rk_{V*}(k_U^*A),\quad j_V^*Rj_{W*}D\cong Rk_{V*}D,$$
and $Rj_{U*}Rk_{U*}\cong Rj_{W*}$, $Rj_{V*}Rk_{V*}\cong Rj_{W*}$. Here $A,B,D$ are arbitrary objects on the $U,V,W$ slices. The self-restriction identifications are the counits. For $A$ on $U$, define $r_A:Rj_{U*}A\to Rj_{W*}(k_U^*A)$ as the $j_W^*\dashv Rj_{W*}$ transpose of $k_U^*\epsilon_{U,A}$, using canonical iterated restriction; define $r_B$ likewise. The listed identifications carry $r_A|_U$ and $r_B|_V$ to the respective units for $k_U^*\dashv Rk_{U*}$ and $k_V^*\dashv Rk_{V*}$, carry $r_B|_U$ and $r_A|_V$ to the identity under the cross-identifications, and carry $r_A|_W,r_B|_W$ to identities under the self-restriction counits. All comparisons are induced on K-injective representatives by the sectionwise product identifications and preserve these adjunction maps.

proof.text: Use Mathlib overPushforwardOverAdj and overMapPushforwardAdj for the actual module restriction and direct-image functors. Apply prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist on the ambient site and each slice. Its Grothendieck-abelian assertion and the source-library HasKInjectiveResolutions instance provide monomorphic K-injective resolutions.

Use the existing exactness declarations overFunctor_exact_ofUniverses and overMap_exact_ofUniverses. Apply lem-sp-site-restriction-kinjective-independent-ring and lem-sp-site-relocalization-kinjective-independent-ring to restriction; apply lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective to each ordinary restriction/direct-image adjunction.

Construct each DerivedPair using source-library mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction, exact restriction mapDerivedCategoryFactors, and rightDerivedFunctorUnit. The latter is invertible on K-injectives. The derived unit factorization derivedη_fac_app and the ordinary termwise adjunction prove the required chain-transpose equation. Transposing the chain counit gives the derived counit normalization.

Construct the two restriction compositors by exactDerivedRestrictionComposition applied to overFunctorMap. Its factorization equation, with the identity complex compositor cancelled degreewise, proves CompositionNormalization for each independently chosen derived-category universe.

Subterminality makes Over.forget full, hence its adjunction unit is invertible. The module direct-image counit is restriction along this unit, so it is invertible; the normalized derived counit is then invertible on K-injective representatives and hence everywhere. For each cross map apply lem-sp-ringed-topos-ordinary-cross-restriction degreewise. The transpose and compositor normalizations identify the derived overlap on K-injectives with this chain map. Exact restriction transfers the isomorphism to the derived category, and resolutions transfer it to every object.

Define the W-to-U and W-to-V comparisons as the adjunction mates of inverse restriction composition followed by the W-counit. They are isomorphisms because conjugateIsoEquiv identifies composite right adjoints and the U,V counits are isomorphisms. Define the cross comparisons by restricted overlap followed by these mates. Their explicit mate formulas follow from homEquiv naturality and the defining overlap transpose. Define composite comparisons by conjugateIsoEquiv. The six overlap identities follow from homEquiv inverse identities, naturality, and the adjunction triangle identities. These formal calculations provide every field of Comparisons.

No covering hypothesis is needed, and subterminality is used only in two places: the graph and the first projection are inverse on T×U for T→U, and T×W≅T×_U W. I checked all 9 steps by hand. Step 1: the module version of the 03CE/trf slice formula has R(T)→R(T×Z)→R(T) equal to the identity, its two transpose formulas are mutually inverse, and its counit is restriction along the graph. Step 2: the hypotheses of the 08BJ criterion hold, applied first to extension by zero ⊣ restriction and then to restriction ⊣ direct image. Step 3: 070K applies because a termwise additive functor carries cones and shifts to cones and shifts (014X, argued in the step). Step 4: the derived adjunction follows from the 070I bijections. Its counit is the ordinary counit at a K-injective I. Its unit is the ordinary one when M is K-injective, which the step correctly requires. Steps 5-6: the product identifications T×_U(U×V)≅T×V, T×W≅T×_U W and (C×U)×_U W≅C×W hold, and the scalar actions agree. Step 7: the derived comparisons hold on K-injective representatives, because k_V^*J and k_{U*}L are K-injective. Step 8: I recomputed the transpose of ρ_I; it is k_U^*ε, since T→T×W→T×U is the graph. Step 9: on U the map is the unit, ρ_J is the identity under the cross identifications, and on W both maps are identities by the triangle identity.
